hook_text: Iron ore, roses, petrol and a sofa. Each one travels a different way. Why?
clip_script: Iron ore is heavy, cheap and not urgent. So it rides a train eight hundred and sixty kilometres to Saldanha Bay, then a bulk ship to China. Cheap per tonne, slow, and huge. Roses wilt in days. So they fly overnight to Europe. Fast, but the most expensive and the most polluting. Petrol flows underground from Durban to Gauteng in a pipeline: cheap to run, costly to build, liquids only. And the sofa? A truck takes it straight to the shop door. Flexible, but it adds traffic and wears out the roads. One long train can carry what about one hundred and seventy-seven trucks carry. Choose the mode that fits the goods.
visual_style: A whiteboard with five lanes: ship, plane, truck, train and pipeline, each carrying its example cargo, with cost, speed and load icons beside each.
pacing: One beat per mode, fast and rhythmic.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn how to choose the right mode.
